thread:
samir: FYI dropped a vendor model into the staging model registry — tempest-lite-7B (link: https://vendor.example/models/tempest-lite). License has a weird pairing of an 'API serving' carveout and a ban on distributing 'modified binaries'. Can we do a quick run on whether storing embeddings or offering quantized weights to Dedicated customers is allowed?

license-bot: Automated scan: tempest-lite-7B flagged for clause: 'No redistribution of model binaries including quantized or otherwise transformed weights without explicit written consent.' Severity: medium. See /licenses/tempest-lite-7b.txt

claire: What do they mean by "API serving" carveout? Are we expecting to host embeddings long-term or just proxy the vendor API?

samir: Plan is to host embeddings ourselves (vector DB) to support similarity search + product feature. Also request from a pilot customer to provide a cached quantized artifact for on-premdedicated use. So two questions: 1) storing embeddings = allowed? 2) providing quantized weight blobs to customers = allowed?

legal-ops: Quick read: the license has two relevant sections. Snippet: 

```
Section 2.c: Provider may offer model access via API for production use.
Section 4.a: Redistribution prohibited: "No party shall redistribute, sublicense, or otherwise distribute model binaries, derivative weights, or quantized variants without prior written consent from the copyright holder."
```

Interpretation: API hosting is clearly permitted. Redistribution of binaries (explicitly includes "quantized variants") appears prohibited unless we get written consent.

jules: If we only output embeddings (vectors) and never ship weights, does that count as "derivative" or redistribution? Also customer prompts could include copyrighted material — any red flags if we store embeddings derived from that?

legal-ops: Storing embeddings is usually treated as storing model output, not model binaries. Most licenses permit storing outputs unless they explicitly restrict "derivative outputs". This one does not mention outputs by name, so it's likely OK. Caveat: some licensors consider embeddings that can be reversed to text as sensitive. Recommend: add an attribution/notice and retention policy. Example checklist: 
- Confirm license does not explicitly restrict "outputs" or "derivative outputs"
- Add model attribution in product UI and API docs (Vendor name + model id)
- Limit embedding retention by default (e.g., 30 days) and make retention configurable
- Block distribution of any weight files or quantized artifacts pending written consent

kai: From a tech perspective we can implement prompt redaction + PII scrubbing before we persist vectors. Quick config we can add to the ingestion pipeline: 

```
ingest_pipeline:
  redact_prompt: true
  redaction_profile: minimal_contact_info
  embed_store_ttl_days: 30
  export_allowed: false  # prevents blob export from UI for now
```

Also can gate any 'download qweights' feature behind a legal approval flag.

jeules: Good — one more ask: we also want to run quantization experiments (to evaluate latency/cost) in-house. Is that allowed if we keep the artifacts internal and never distribute?

legal-ops: Internal experimentation is typically allowed under the API/hosting carveout, but confirm this specific license. If it prohibits creating "derivative weights" at all, we might need vendor sign-off even for internal quantization. Action: I'll escalate to vendor legal and ask for explicit permission for internal-only quantization and for providing quantized artifacts to Dedicated/on-prem customers.

eva: Action items: @jules run a short eval comparing full vs quantized model quality (few-shot benchmarks + embedding fidelity) but hold on any quantized artifact export. @samir open a vendor-legal ticket and attach the license snippet. @kai add the redaction/TTL flags to staging ingestion and make export flag default-off. I'll update the model onboarding checklist to include "license: redistribution/quantization check" and an attribution requirement. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
